name: Velastrin
description: A licensed SNT-interface sensitizer that amplifies tactile and proprioceptive feedback from chrome augments, making mechanical limbs and sensory implants feel dramatically more 'present' and responsive. Medically prescribed for augment integration therapy — helping patients reconnect with their chrome after trauma or rejection episodes. Widely used recreationally for the sensation of feeling one's augments as extensions of self rather than attachments.
effects: Tactile feedback from augmented limbs amplified to near-organic sensitivity
Proprioceptive clarity — augments feel precisely located in space
Sensory augments report increased subjective richness of input
Emotional warmth associated with augmented body parts — reduced body dysmorphia
Enhanced fine motor control through improved feedback loops
side_effects: Hypersensitivity — augments become painfully responsive to impact or pressure
Emotional distress if augments are damaged or removed while dosed
Mild physical dependency with prolonged use
Rebound dissociation upon cessation — augments feel 'dead' for 12-24 hours
Contraindicated with combat-grade chrome due to pain feedback risk in injury
cultural_context: Velastrin sits at a cultural intersection in GLMZ. For augmented Tier 2 workers who've had chrome for years and stopped feeling it, Velastrin is a way to reclaim their body. For Tier 3 users with high-end cosmetic augments, it's an experience drug — feeling expensive chrome the way it was meant to feel. There's a quiet, melancholy community of long-term augmented users who take Velastrin not to get high, but to feel whole. Therapists debate whether this is healthy adaptation or dependency.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 augment therapist is prescribing Velastrin far beyond medical need — their patients are becoming dependent, but they genuinely believe the drug is therapeutic. Someone wants the therapist stopped, and it's not clear if the motive is ethical or commercial.

A Shelf fighter with extensive combat chrome has never taken Velastrin and doesn't know what they're missing — being given it for the first time mid-mission causes an unexpected emotional crisis when they feel, for the first time, how much of their original body is gone
Counterfeit Velastrin is circulating that includes a hidden secondary compound — one that makes users' augment feedback vulnerable to external BCI signal hijacking
